title: Pistachio nougat
subtitle: firm honey nougat with whole pistachios, sliced into bars
excerpt: Pistachio nougat is a sweet of cooked sugar and honey beaten into stiff egg whites and set with a generous handful of pistachios. The sugar must reach hard ball stage, 140 degrees C, before it goes into the egg whites; this temperature gives a firm nougat that slices cleanly into bars rather than a soft, chewy one. The nougat is pressed into a lined tin to set overnight.
sourceNotes: Nougat documented throughout the Mediterranean and Middle East as one of the oldest sugar confections. The Italian torrone and French nougat de Montelimar are the most well-known versions. The method of beating hot sugar syrup into egg whites derives from Italian meringue technique applied to confectionery.

glossaryTerms.definition: A sugar cooking stage reached at 130 to 145 degrees C. A small amount of syrup dropped into cold water forms a hard ball that is slightly pliable but holds its shape firmly. Used for nougat and marshmallow; the exact temperature determines how firm the result will be.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps wrapped in baking paper at room temperature in an airtight tin for up to 2 weeks. Do not refrigerate; moisture from the fridge makes the nougat sticky.
recipe.temperatureNote: hard ball stage (140 degrees C) for a firm, sliceable nougat

content.text: Pistachio nougat is a confection of cooked sugar beaten into stiff egg whites. The sugar syrup must reach
at 140 degrees C before it goes into the whites; this temperature gives a nougat that slices cleanly into bars. A stand mixer is essential: you need both hands free when pouring the hot syrup.
The nougat is pressed into a lined tin to set overnight. Cutting it while still slightly warm with an oiled knife gives the cleanest slices.
Line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper, leaving an overhang on two sides.

Put the caster sugar, glucose syrup, honey, and water into a medium saucepan. Stir over a low heat until the sugar dissolves. Stop stirring, increase the heat to medium-high, and clip a sugar thermometer to the side of the pan.
Cook without stirring until the syrup reaches 140 degrees C.
While the syrup is cooking, beat the egg whites in the stand mixer on high speed until they hold firm, stiff peaks. Keep the mixer running on low.

As soon as the syrup reaches 140 degrees C, remove from the heat. With the mixer running on medium speed, pour the hot syrup into the egg whites in a thin, steady stream down the inside of the bowl. Avoid pouring directly onto the whisk attachment.

Once all the syrup is in, increase the speed to high and beat for 6 to 8 minutes until the mixture is thick, stiff, and has cooled to near room temperature. It should hold a firm shape when you stop the mixer.
Fold in the pistachios with a silicone spatula. The mixture will be very stiff; work quickly before it sets.
Scrape into the lined tin. Press down into an even layer with lightly oiled baking paper placed over the top. Leave at room temperature overnight to set.
Lift out using the baking paper overhang. Cut into bars with a sharp, lightly oiled knife. Wrap each bar in a square of baking paper.

attrs.problem: Nougat too soft and sticky after setting overnight
attrs.avoid: Avoid under-cooking the syrup; syrup below 140 degrees C gives a nougat that never sets firm enough to slice.
attrs.fix: Check the thermometer is accurate. There is no way to rescue soft nougat once mixed with the egg whites, but it makes a good spread or dip for fruit.

attrs.avoid: Avoid stirring the syrup after the sugar has dissolved; stirring promotes crystallisation.
attrs.fix: Brush the inside of the pan above the syrup line with a wet pastry brush a few times during cooking to dissolve any sugar crystals that form on the sides.

attrs.problem: Mixture sets too quickly before all the nuts are added
attrs.avoid: Avoid beating the mixture beyond the point where it loses its sheen and becomes very stiff.
attrs.fix: Have the pistachios ready and weighed before you start. Add them as soon as the beating is done and work very fast to fold through before the nougat stiffens.
